Constrained stacking weights from response-scale predictions

stack_weights_response.Rd

The simplex-constrained counterpart of stacking_gaussian, stacking_binomial and stacking_poisson: it minimises the same family loss under the constraint \(w \ge 0\), \(\sum_j w_j = 1\), where the stacked prediction is the convex combination \(\mu_i = \sum_j w_j y_{ij}\) on the RESPONSE scale.

Usage

stack_weights_response(
  Y,
  z,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson"),
  w_init = NULL,
  kkt_tol = 1e-08,
  eps = 1e-08
)

Arguments

Y

An n x m matrix of external predictions on the response scale: probabilities for binomial, positive rates for poisson.

z

The target response, length n.

family

One of "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson".

w_init

Optional starting weights; defaults to equal weights.

kkt_tol

Stopping tolerance on the KKT residual.

eps

Clamp keeping binomial probabilities inside [eps, 1 - eps] and poisson rates above eps, so the loss stays finite at the boundary.

Value

A list with weights, constrained (always TRUE), fitted, value, kkt and iters.

Details

Losses and their gradients, with \(\partial Q/\partial w_k = \sum_i (\partial Q/\partial \mu_i) y_{ik}\):

gaussian

\(Q = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_i (z_i - \mu_i)^2\), \(\partial Q/\partial \mu_i = \mu_i - z_i\)

binomial

\(Q = -\sum_i [z_i \log p_i + (1 - z_i)\log(1 - p_i)]\), \(\partial Q/\partial p_i = (p_i - z_i)/(p_i(1 - p_i))\)

poisson

\(Q = \sum_i [\mu_i - z_i \log \mu_i]\), \(\partial Q/\partial \mu_i = 1 - z_i/\mu_i\)

Each loss is convex in \(\mu\) and \(\mu\) is linear in \(w\), so the problem is convex on the simplex and the projected-gradient solution is the global optimum, certified by the KKT residual rather than by a stalled objective.

A softmax reparameterisation \(w_k = e^{\alpha_k}/\sum_j e^{\alpha_j}\) reaches the same optimum and was used to derive these gradients independently; it is not used here because it cannot put a weight exactly at zero and because it carries a flat direction (adding a constant to every alpha leaves w unchanged).
